summary: The draft has the Boston Connor cadence (short blunt sentences, FRAUD/UNBELIEVABLE, five-step recaps, no hometown bias) and the right lead story, but the lead attaches Geno Smith's 287 yards to Miami's win when he is the Jets quarterback in that game.

items.evidence: Opinions land as settled: “That's how you lose a week.” (lead); “They earned every inch of that drop.” (rankings[8]); “which is a lineup you delete.” (rankings[10]); “This is not a puzzle.” (awards, Lineup Crime); “I would have started him out of spite.” (awards)

Real lines, absurd close: Mahomes 165 / Geno 287 → “Superflex is a second quarterback slot, not a museum piece.” then “FRAUD.” (lead); Daniels −0.30 on 6 snaps → “Start a kicker. Start a chair.” (awards); Shrader −1.00 and a win → “One receiver covered a pile of junk.” (recaps[6])

Confrontational: “Who starts 165 yards over 287?” (lead); “so fifth is a gift.” (rankings[5]); “Unserious operation.” (rankings[4]). UC gets it: “the sponsor started Jaylin Noel for two catches and minus-3 yards.” (rankings[6]); “The sponsor found a new disaster.” (recaps[5]); “The sponsor did not do his.” (awards). Self-deprecating: “I don't make the rules. I just watch people ignore them.” (lead); “Correct, unfortunately.” (rankings[1])
No wink: “FRAUD.” (lead); “This is not a puzzle.” (awards); “I would have started him out of spite.” (awards) after hammball still won by 34.42. Nothing walks it back.

Declarative snaps dominate: “That's how you lose a week.” “Zero touchdowns. One pick.” “From the bench. 23.48 points.” “FRAUD.” (lead); “About time.” (recaps[1]); “This was not a game.” (recaps[4]); “Bad draw. Worse bench.” (recaps[2]); “It was enough.” (recaps[6])

Yards and the 2.88 margin, then “Who starts 165 yards over 287? Superflex is a second quarterback slot, not a museum piece.” (lead); Love/Doubs/Daniels zeros, then “Start people who play. Wild idea.” (recaps[3]); Jones 3.62 and two minus-1.00s, then “One receiver covered a pile of junk.” (recaps[6])
Used occasionally, implying everyone else is an idiot: “Who starts 165 yards over 287?” (lead); “What are you saving him for?” (recaps[5]). “I have questions.” (transactions) stays rare.

Wild takes in the calm of fact: “Superflex is a second quarterback slot, not a museum piece. … I don't make the rules.” (lead); “which is a lineup you delete.” (rankings[10]); “Start a chair.” (awards); “fifth is a gift.” (rankings[5]). All still read as opinion.
Two real outbursts: “FRAUD.” (lead) and “UNBELIEVABLE.” (recaps[3]). WELL! is the team name. No other ALL CAPS yelling.

Lead stays dry through Mahomes 19 of 33 for 165, Geno 23 of 30 for 287, and 113.72 to 116.60, then jumps to the museum-piece read and “FRAUD.” Recaps[3] goes from the Love/Doubs/Daniels lines to “Wild idea.” Recaps[6] lists Shrader, SF DEF, and Jones, then “pile of junk.”

Dismissive closes instead of lectures: “FRAUD.” (lead); “Start the skill players. It works.” (recaps[1]); “Worse bench.” (recaps[2]); “Wild idea.” (recaps[3]); “Bring a team next time.” (recaps[4]); “It was enough.” (recaps[6]); “Do that.” / “This is not a puzzle.” (awards)

Unpolished fan talk: “That's how you lose a week.” “From the couch” (rankings[4]); “pile of junk” (recaps[6]); “Gift-wrapped.” (waivers); “Unserious operation.” (rankings[4]); “Hell of a supporting cast.” (recaps[5])
Insults and slang: “FRAUD.”, “new disaster”, “pile of junk”, “lineup you delete”, “Unserious operation.” One swear: “Hell of a supporting cast.” (recaps[5])
Placed, not sprayed: “FRAUD.” (lead); “UNBELIEVABLE.” (recaps[3]); “The sponsor found a new disaster.” (recaps[5]). No carpet-bomb of bum/pathetic/embarrassing.

Comparisons that don't survive a second look: “not a museum piece” (lead); “Start a chair.” (awards); “One receiver covered a pile of junk.” (recaps[6]); “which is a lineup you delete.” (rankings[10])
No academic transitions or long metaphors: “About time.” “This was not a game.” “Bad draw. Worse bench.” “Gift-wrapped.” “Messy. Coin flip.” “museum piece” is a short fan jab, not an extended figure.

Questionable takes as law: “That's how you lose a week.” (lead); “I don't make the rules.” (lead); “They earned every inch of that drop.” (rankings[8]); “This is not a puzzle.” (awards); “Split, if they learned anything.” (preview)

Confident arguments that sag: yards-in as a Superflex statute (“I don't make the rules.”) (lead); “Ted Hurst caught zero balls on one target and they're third.” (rankings[3]); winning with Shrader at −1.00 treated as the method (recaps[6]); Daniels at −0.30 → “Start a chair.” (awards)

Craziest lines in a flat voice: “I don't make the rules. I just watch people ignore them.” (lead); “Start a chair.” (awards); “116.60 is a bad score. It was enough.” (recaps[6]); “which is a lineup you delete.” (rankings[10])

Dry swap math to “FRAUD.” (lead); recaps[3] opens already hot (“UNBELIEVABLE.”) then the zeros; recaps[5] goes from Pollard's 36.50 to “The sponsor found a new disaster.” Rankings[10] climbs from Love/Doubs/Daniels to “a lineup you delete.”

Detail, then a short insult: “FRAUD.” (lead); “It works.” (recaps[1]); “Worse bench.” (recaps[2]); “Wild idea.” (recaps[3]); “Bring a team next time.” (recaps[4]); “Hell of a supporting cast.” (recaps[5]); “It was enough.” (recaps[6])

Defends the roast after the evidence cuts against it: Pollard 36.50 from the couch “and they still rose. … Unserious operation.” (rankings[4]); “You sat 36.50 and won anyway. … What are you saving him for?” (recaps[5]); “I would have started him out of spite.” after the 34.42 win (awards); “116.60 is a bad score. It was enough.” (recaps[6])

items.evidence: “Geno Smith went 23 of 30 for 287 yards and three scores in Miami's 28-25 win.” (lead.body) attaches Split's bench QB to Miami. brief.json lists Geno Smith as NYJ, opponent MIA, nfl_game “MIA 28, NYJ 25”; the ESPN recap under that game has Jets QB Geno Smith 23 of 30 for 287 yards.

Irrational bits read as takes: “not a museum piece”, “I don't make the rules”, “FRAUD.”, “Start a chair.”, “lineup you delete.” ESPN-only claims are sourced: “First defeat of the season for the Chiefs, per ESPN.”; Love “out a second week with a sore ankle”; Pollard's career-high-tying scores; Javonte's best rushing night; McCarthy's first start. No invented trades, firings, or quotes.

Straight carriers sit next to the jokes: “Mahomes went 19 of 33 for 165 yards in Kansas City's 20-3 loss at Seattle.” “Split lost 113.72 to 116.60. The margin was 2.88.” “Quinshon Judkins ran for 96 yards and two scores.” Injury notes and standout lines stay factual.
Caps twice in the issue (“FRAUD.”, “UNBELIEVABLE.”). No signature line repeated. “What are you saving him for?” appears once in recaps[5] (the award is a title, not a second catchphrase in prose).

Comic energy without hometown bias: short blunt openers, absurd reads (“museum piece”, “Start a chair.”), five-step lead and recaps, UC roasted as the sponsor. No Patriots/Fenway/“this state” framing; Maye, Stevenson, and CHI 30, NE 24 appear only as real box-score facts.

notes.quote: Geno Smith went 23 of 30 for 287 yards and three scores in Miami's 28-25 win.
notes.problem: Same paragraph pattern as “Mahomes went 19 of 33 for 165 yards in Kansas City's 20-3 loss at Seattle,” which names the player's team. Geno is NYJ, not MIA. brief.json: Geno Smith nfl_team NYJ, opponent MIA, nfl_game “MIA 28, NYJ 25.” ESPN recap (MIA 28, NYJ 25): “Smith was 23 of 30 for 287 yards and three touchdowns” as the Jets quarterback in a loss. facts.md: a number attached to the wrong team is a factual error.
notes.fix: Keep 23 of 30, 287 yards, three scores, 23.48, and the 28-25 score, but pin them on the Jets (e.g. “in the Jets' 28-25 loss to Miami”). Do not describe Geno as playing in Miami's win.

notes.quote: parked Omar Cooper's 5 catches, 115 yards, and a touchdown on the bench. That's 62.10 sitting down in a 31.16 loss.
notes.problem: 62.10 is ThePeopleBeaters' bench total (Cooper 22.50 plus Wilson, Flournoy, Allen, Freiermuth). Sitting right after Cooper's line, it can read as Cooper's points.
notes.fix: Name the bench: “The bench was 62.10 in a 31.16 loss,” or split Cooper's 22.50 from the 62.10 total.

notes.quote: The sponsor found a new disaster. Hell of a supporting cast.
notes.problem: The unit opens on hammball sitting Pollard's 36.50; the punchline pivots to UC's Noel. The closer should still slap the bench crime the recap started with.
notes.fix: Keep the Noel disaster if you want the sponsor roast, but land the last line on sitting 36.50 / 108.18 and still winning.
